body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and publish to npm yourself or [setup this action to publish automatically](https://github.com/changesets/action#with-publishing). If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## @objectstack/spec@18.3.0

### Minor Changes

- 21a13f1: spec(ui): a navigation group that says nothing opens — `GroupNavItem.expanded` defaults to `true`
  
  Clause-②: yes
  Metadata-protocol: semantic
  
  <!-- adr-0087: registered ui-nav-group-expanded-default-open -->
  
  **BREAKING** — a declared default moves, shipped as `minor` under the launch-window convention. The author who relied on the documented default (`false`, "a group starts collapsed unless the author opens it") for a group meant to stay out of the daily user's sight — an advanced, developer or diagnostics section — now sees it open on first view wherever the app is parsed (`defineStack`, `defineApp`, a compiled `objectstack.json`). The remedy is one key on that group: `expanded: false`.
  
  - **Before.** `GroupNavItemSchema.expanded` defaulted to `false`. An app parsed through `defineStack` or `defineApp` (and so every compiled `objectstack.json`) carried a written `expanded: false` on every group whose author said nothing. The console honours a written `false` as an explicit close, so those groups started collapsed. An app registered without a parse (the platform's Setup and Account apps) arrived without the key, and the console opened its groups. The protocol and the console disagreed about what a silent group means.
  - **Now.** The default is `true`. A group that says nothing parses to `expanded: true` and opens on first view, the same answer the console already gave a group without the key. A group holding the current route still opens whatever it declares.
  - **To keep a group closed**, write `expanded: false`. Setup's Advanced group and Account's Developer group already do, and they still collapse. Every authored `expanded` parses exactly as before, and a non-boolean is still refused.
  - **Compiled artifacts.** A document that serialised an earlier parse (an `os compile` artifact) carries the old written `false`, and its groups stay closed. Recompile it, or delete the key.
  - **Upgrade path.** The ADR-0087 D3 semantic entry `ui-nav-group-expanded-default-open` carries the change to `os migrate meta` and the upgrade guide. The default change is declared in the build's default-change ledger. No key is added or removed.
- 43714ca: feat(spec): an import row result can report every cell error of a failed row in `errors`
  
  Clause-②: yes (widening)
  Metadata-protocol: added
  
  `ImportRowResultSchema` (and so `ImportResponseSchema.results` and the async job's `results` sample) declares one optional member, `errors`: an array with one element per failed cell of a failed row, in the validate verdict's issue shape (`ValidateDataIssueSchema`: `field`, `code`, `message`), the same element the row's `warnings` already uses. The list holds the import's cell-coercion errors, and a cell error never carries the advisory-only `rule` or `severity`. It is present only on a failed row that has at least one cell error. The first-error keys `field`, `code` and `error` stay and keep naming element 0, so every current reader sees the same answer. Before, the schema had no such key, so `ImportRowResultSchema.parse` would strip one. This is the contract half: the import runner fills `errors` in a later change, and until then no server sends it.

## @objectstack/service-automation@18.3.0

### Patch Changes

- 2282aa8: feat(trigger-schedule): a scheduled run whose due time passed while no kernel was ticking is recorded as `missed` in the flow's run history, and is not run
  
  Clause-②: yes (widening)
  Metadata-protocol: none
  
  A hosted kernel that is stopped, evicted or restarting does not tick, and a scheduled flow due in that gap used to leave no trace: nothing ran and nothing said so, so an app could not tell a sweep had not happened. Now the next kernel to bind the flow records each such due time once, as a run-history entry with status `missed`:
  
  - **What the entry says.** `startedAt` is the due time that passed and `completedAt` the instant the next kernel detected it. No step ran, so `steps` is empty; `trigger.type` is `schedule`. The entry is listed by `listRuns` (and `GET /api/v1/automation/:name/runs`), `?status=missed` selects it, and it is durable history in `sys_automation_run`, aged out like every other terminal run.
  - **Record only.** Nothing is run for a missed due time. It is never replayed or caught up; the flow's next due time runs as usual.
  - **What counts as a silence.** The flow's job was still armed when its kernel stopped (its `sys_job` row still `active`: a kernel that stops ticking cancels nothing, while disabling, republishing or withdrawing a flow does), and a due time of the schedule that kernel armed falls after its last fire and before the next kernel bound the flow. A kernel that ticked through records nothing, and a flow that was deliberately unbound records nothing for the time it was unbound.
  - **A refusal is not a silence.** A kernel that refuses the flow on purpose (scheduled work switched off for it, a missing acting organization, an unreadable schedule) now disarms the job by its name even when it never bound it, so the next kernel to run the flow does not read that kernel's life as missed due times. `FlowTrigger` gains an optional `release(flowName)`, which the engine calls when its scheduled-work policy refuses a flow before the trigger is reached.
  - **Never a run that happened.** A due time whose tick window is claimed in the dispatch ledger (`sys_flow_dispatch`) was dispatched, landed or died in flight, and is not recorded. With no persisted ledger the check is skipped, and a ledger read that fails records nothing for that due time; the trigger says either at `warn`, naming the flow.
  - **Bounded by the run history's own cap.** At most the run history's per-flow cap (`maxTerminalRunsPerFlow`, 100 by default) of the newest due times are recorded per flow per detection, since the store keeps no more terminal rows than that per flow. One `warn` line names the flow, how many earlier due times were not recorded and the earliest of them.
  - **Two replicas, one row.** The entry's id is derived from the flow and the due time, so replicas that detect the same silence write one history row.
  
  `DbJobAdapter` gains `readArming(name)` (adapter-local, like `setReplayGuard`; not part of `IJobService`), which reads how a job's `sys_job` row was left. `AutomationEngine` gains `recordMissedRun(...)` and `missedRunLimit()`, the run stores expose their configured `maxTerminalRunsPerFlow`, and `TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES` and the `sys_automation_run.status` options gain `missed`.

## @objectstack/service-job@18.3.0

### Patch Changes

- 2282aa8: feat(trigger-schedule): a scheduled run whose due time passed while no kernel was ticking is recorded as `missed` in the flow's run history, and is not run
  
  Clause-②: yes (widening)
  Metadata-protocol: none
  
  A hosted kernel that is stopped, evicted or restarting does not tick, and a scheduled flow due in that gap used to leave no trace: nothing ran and nothing said so, so an app could not tell a sweep had not happened. Now the next kernel to bind the flow records each such due time once, as a run-history entry with status `missed`:
  
  - **What the entry says.** `startedAt` is the due time that passed and `completedAt` the instant the next kernel detected it. No step ran, so `steps` is empty; `trigger.type` is `schedule`. The entry is listed by `listRuns` (and `GET /api/v1/automation/:name/runs`), `?status=missed` selects it, and it is durable history in `sys_automation_run`, aged out like every other terminal run.
  - **Record only.** Nothing is run for a missed due time. It is never replayed or caught up; the flow's next due time runs as usual.
  - **What counts as a silence.** The flow's job was still armed when its kernel stopped (its `sys_job` row still `active`: a kernel that stops ticking cancels nothing, while disabling, republishing or withdrawing a flow does), and a due time of the schedule that kernel armed falls after its last fire and before the next kernel bound the flow. A kernel that ticked through records nothing, and a flow that was deliberately unbound records nothing for the time it was unbound.
  - **A refusal is not a silence.** A kernel that refuses the flow on purpose (scheduled work switched off for it, a missing acting organization, an unreadable schedule) now disarms the job by its name even when it never bound it, so the next kernel to run the flow does not read that kernel's life as missed due times. `FlowTrigger` gains an optional `release(flowName)`, which the engine calls when its scheduled-work policy refuses a flow before the trigger is reached.
  - **Never a run that happened.** A due time whose tick window is claimed in the dispatch ledger (`sys_flow_dispatch`) was dispatched, landed or died in flight, and is not recorded. With no persisted ledger the check is skipped, and a ledger read that fails records nothing for that due time; the trigger says either at `warn`, naming the flow.
  - **Bounded by the run history's own cap.** At most the run history's per-flow cap (`maxTerminalRunsPerFlow`, 100 by default) of the newest due times are recorded per flow per detection, since the store keeps no more terminal rows than that per flow. One `warn` line names the flow, how many earlier due times were not recorded and the earliest of them.
  - **Two replicas, one row.** The entry's id is derived from the flow and the due time, so replicas that detect the same silence write one history row.
  
  `DbJobAdapter` gains `readArming(name)` (adapter-local, like `setReplayGuard`; not part of `IJobService`), which reads how a job's `sys_job` row was left. `AutomationEngine` gains `recordMissedRun(...)` and `missedRunLimit()`, the run stores expose their configured `maxTerminalRunsPerFlow`, and `TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES` and the `sys_automation_run.status` options gain `missed`.
